route.name: The Cold Granite, Rungs & Mountain-Machine Loop
route.direction: Boston up the Maine coast through Portsmouth, Portland, Bath and Rockland to Acadia and Bangor, then west through Bethel and the White Mountains into Vermont and south through Killington and Woodstock to Manchester and Boston
route.summary: Northern New England as physical material: an experimental submarine, a working lobster boat, Navy destroyer construction from land and river, giant forest trolls, a granite breakwater, a memorial cliff, Cadillac at dawn, iron rungs on the Beehive, a Stephen King field tour, Moon and Mars rock, the exact-date wife carrying championship, a cog railway to 6,288 feet, a Vermont canopy course, a last-day mountain coaster and gondola, boulder caves and two Frank Lloyd Wright houses.

constraints.route_specific_drive_rule: No planned uninterrupted run exceeds roughly 2.5 hours. The measured worst case is the Skowhegan to Bethel leg.
constraints.visa_policy: US-only route with no border crossing. The 2026 Acadia non-US-resident entrance structure must be checked against each traveler's status before purchase.

experience_model.design_rule: Optional, flex, archived and alternative originals stay visible but never affect Magic unless the group activates them.
experience_model.museum_like_note: The Maine Mineral & Gem Museum is the single passive museum. It survives because lunar and Martian material in a small western-Maine town is route-defining, and on a 25-stop route one museum is 4%.
experience_model.texture_note: The brief groups CHALLENGE and COMPETE as a single row of two; this package records them separately as ArborTrek and the Beast coaster.

notes: Shopping is deliberately taken on arrival day so it never interrupts the mountain and foliage blocks later.
